passage: I'm Asif. Before the maths test, Karthik sat next to me wringing his hands, one over the other, again and again. I thought he must be nervous. I almost said nothing because I didn't want to make it worse. Then I whispered, “You okay?” He said, “I always forget the formulas.” I said, “Me too. Want to go through the area one quickly?” We did it for two minutes, and his hands stopped. I don't know if that was the only reason, because it was cold in the room too. But it helped a bit.

qa.q: What was Karthik doing with his hands before the test?
qa.a: He was wringing his hands, one over the other, again and again.

qa.q: What did Asif think Karthik was feeling, and how sure can he be?
qa.a: He thought Karthik was nervous, and Karthik said he always forgets the formulas, which fits. Asif admits he cannot be sure, since the room was also cold.
Asif asked quietly if he was okay and offered to go through the formula together, which gave Karthik something concrete to do.

qa.q: How might Karthik feel when Asif whispered to him?
qa.a: Probably relieved that somebody noticed and did not make a fuss, and less alone with his worry.

grounding: A child sees a classmate wring the hands before a test, reads nervousness, and offers a friendly word.

passage: Note from Hafsa, Class 5 teacher. Before the spelling test I saw Noor wringing her hands under the desk. I could not tell if she was nervous or just cold from the fan. I bent down and asked quietly how she felt about the test. She said, “I keep thinking I'll go blank.” I told her she could take a slow breath and begin with the words she knows best. Her hands loosened. I did not tell the class. I will check in with her privately before the next test and ask what helped.

qa.q: Where did Hafsa see Noor wringing her hands?
qa.a: She saw Noor wringing her hands under the desk.

qa.q: What was Noor most likely feeling, and what else could explain her hands?
qa.a: Most likely she was nervous about going blank in the test, as she told Hafsa. Cold from the fan could also have made her wring her hands.

qa.q: What did Hafsa do that helped, and what will she do next?
qa.a: She asked quietly and privately and offered a way to start, and she will check in before the next test to ask what helped.

qa.q: How might Hafsa feel when Noor's hands loosen?
qa.a: Hafsa is probably relieved that the quiet advice helped, and plans to check in with Noor privately before the next test.

grounding: Wringing hands before a test suggests nervousness though it does not prove it; a friendly word helps.
